title: Discovering how populations change
summary: Learn how the population of a place changes and how people live in villages, towns and cities.
keyIdeas: A population is all the people living in a place or territory.
Births, deaths, emigration and immigration change a population.
People can be economically active or inactive, depending on whether they work or look for paid work.

basicKnowledge: C. Sociedades y territorios › Retos del mundo actual

activities.prompt: The total population is the number of people living in a place.
activities.explanation: Total population counts the people living in a territory. It is not always the same as the number listed in an official register.

activities.prompt: What is the council's official record of the people living in a municipality called?
activities.explanation: The municipal population register records the people living in a municipality.
activities.hint: It is an official council record.

activities.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence.
activities.explanation: An emigrant leaves their place of origin to live somewhere else.
activities.sentence: When someone leaves their home village to live in another country, the term for them from that village's point of view is ___.

activities.prompt: Match each population term to its meaning.
activities.explanation: Births and immigration add to the population. Deaths and emigration reduce it.

pairs.right: Number of babies born in a year
Number of people who die in a year
People arriving to live in a place

activities.prompt: Sort these people by their work situation.
activities.explanation: In these examples, people who work or look for a job are economically active. The child and the retired person who is not looking for work are economically inactive.

items.text: Lucía, who works as a municipal firefighter
Hugo, who is 8 and attends primary school
Aisha, who is looking for a job as a hospital doctor
Omar's grandfather, who has retired from his job

activities.prompt: In Nerea's village, 15 babies were born and 9 people died this year. What was the natural population change?
activities.explanation: Natural population change is births minus deaths: 15 − 9 = 6. To find the total population change, we must also count people arriving and leaving.

activities.prompt: Sort these features into rural or urban populations.
activities.explanation: Rural populations live in villages and countryside areas. Urban populations live in towns and cities with many services and industries. These examples show common patterns.

items.text: People living in small, quiet villages
Many people working in factories and offices
Residents mainly working in farming or keeping livestock

activities.prompt: Put this village's story in order using the time clues.
activities.explanation: This is one possible story of population change. Not every village follows the same steps.
items: At first, many young families leave for the city
Then, mainly older people remain and the school closes
Later, new families with children arrive
Finally, the school reopens for those pupils

activities.prompt: Read the story of Valle Verde and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Immigration can bring cultural diversity and help small villages keep their communities and services alive.
activities.title: New neighbours arrive in Valle Verde
activities.text: Valle Verde was a small village with 120 residents. For many years, few babies were born and young people left to study in the city. The school was about to close because it had too few pupils. Last year, however, three families arrived from other countries to work in the farming cooperative. They brought six cheerful children. The villagers held a welcome party in the square. Thanks to their arrival, the village school stays open and children play in the streets again.

questions.prompt: Why was Valle Verde's school about to close?
questions.explanation: Few babies were born and young people left, so the school had too few pupils.
options: There were too few school-age children
The building was very old and dangerous

questions.prompt: The arrival of these families and their children is an example of:
questions.explanation: It is immigration because they come from elsewhere to live and work in Valle Verde.
options: Emigration that reduces the local population
Immigration that helps bring new life to the village

activities.prompt: A municipality had 500 residents in January. During the year, 10 babies were born, 4 people died, 20 people moved in and 6 moved away. How many residents are there at the end of the year?
activities.hint: Add births and arrivals, then subtract deaths and departures.
